5.SMALL FOR GESTATIONAL AGE:

Definitions:

1.Appropriate for Gestational Age:
-Fetal size between 10th and 90th centile.
2.Small for Gest Age (SGA):
-Fetal size < 10 centile.
3.Fetal Growth restriction FGR:
1.Fetal size < 3rd centile.
2.Fetal size <10th centile + Doppler Abnormalities.

(abnormal uterine or Umbilical artery Doppler).

 

⇨Early onset FGR:
-Before 31 + 6 weeks.
1.Fetal size < 10th centile

+

Uterine artery PI > 95th centile

And/or

Umbilical artery PI > 95th centile.

2.Fetal size < 3rd centile

Or

UA – absent end diastolic flow.

 

⇨Late onset FGR:
-> 32 weeks.
1.Fetal size < 10th centile.
2.Fetal size crossing centiles > 2 quartiles on growth centile.
3.Cerebroplacental ratio < 5th centile or UA PI > 95th centile

Or

Fetal size < 3rd centile

4.Static growth:
-No forward Growth velocity in fetal size @ least 14 days apart.
5.FGR in previous Pregnancy:
1.Birth weight < 3rd centile.
2.Early onset pre – eclampsia or FGR requiring birth before 34 weeks.
3.Birth weight < 10 centile with abnormal Doppler studies.
6.LBW:
-Birth weight <2500g.
-This term is no longer used term.
7.Symmetrical & Asymmetrical FGR:
-This classification has no prognostic value but can be related to etiology.
8.Fetal size:
-Measured by AC or EFW (combination of HC, FL, AC).

Risk Factors:

•Maternal Risks.
-Medical conditions – strong association.
-DM with vascular disease.
-Renal disease (moderate & severe).
-APLS.
-Chronic HTN.
-SLE.
•Cardiac conditions (congenital/ CHD).
-Stenotic lesions
-Valvular lesions strong.
-Complex cardiac CHD association

Asthma

Anemia less strong association.

IBD

Depression

•Age > 40.
•BMI < 18.5.
•Gastric bypass (irrespective of BMI).
•Congenital uterine anomalies – septate/ BI corporeal uteri.

Antenatal Risks:

1.Alcohol:
-Small amount – no association.
-1 drink – small association.
-4 drinks – double the risk.
2.Drug Misuse:
-Cocaine esp. crack cocaine. Has
-Marijuana association

So, these should be stopped.

3.Smoking:
-Dose dependent effect more in old women.
-Stopping before 15 weeks – equals to background risk.
⇨Nicotine replacement therapy vs e – cigarettes.

e – cigarettes more effective than NRT.

E – cigarettes less risk of FGR than NRT. Pts with co > 4PPm should be offered further testing for SGA/ FGR on moderate risk.

4.Caffeine consumption:
-300mg/ day in 3rd association with FGR.
-Recommended amount is 200mg/ day.
5.IVF/ ICSI:
-No clear association.
6.Paternal factors no clear association, however changing paternity es risk of pre-eclampsia and FGR
7.Covid – 19:
-Has association severe/ critical women should be offered USG Biometry & further monitoring accordingly.
8.Bleeding in pregnancy except to due to previa has association with FGR/ SGA.
9.Gest hypertension or Pre – Eclampsia.

Aneuploidy Biochemical Markers:

•Low PAPP – A

Or should be offered Aspirin.

•Raised β – HCG

Low PAPP – A

Raised α FP Associations with FGR/SGA

(above 2 MOM) So, Additional

Raised inhibin surveillance is

(above 2 MOM) recommended.

Low PPAP – A => Association with still birth.

β – HCG (above 4 MOM) no association with SGA.

So, no additional surveillance should be done.

 

 

Prevention of FGR:

⇨Reduce smoking – Recommended.
-All women who smoke should be assessed by co levels.
-Ensure in house treatment from + tobacco dependence advisor.
-Use opt out referral process.

⇨Vitamin D 10mg throughout pregnancy Recommended uncertain role.
⇨Folic Acid 400mg pre conception & 1st recommended.
-Prevent other pregnancy complications.
⇨Balanced energy/ protein supplementation:
-birth weight.
-Role is not clear.
⇨Omega 3 long chain poly un saturated fatty acid – No effect.
⇨Minerals, micronutrients & vitamins – not clear.
⇨Calcium supplementation reduces pre – Eclampsia but FGR association not clear.
⇨Aspirin 150mg recommended
-Between 12 – 36 + 6 weeks to those women who are at risk of pre – eclampsia & placental dysfunction.
-It reduces their chance of developing SGA / FGR.
-150mg OD @ night.
⇨LMWH – not recommended.

Surveillance tools for FGR:

⇨Symphisio fundal height SFH:
-Routinely offered after 24 weeks.
-SFH < 10th centile => Refer for USG.
-Serial SFH more informative.
-Plot serial SFH on growth charts.
-3 types of growth charts population base, standard & customized.
-Customized charts improve detection.

 

⇨USG – core component of FGR surveillance.
-Routine USG for AC/EFW don’t improve outcome.
-Fetal size is measured by AC or EFW. AC is superior but inferior to combined measurement leading to EFW.
-EFW is measured by fetal parameters like FL, AC, HC.
-Fetal size should be measured @ least 3 – weeks by headlock formula, in SGA every 2 weeks.
-Plotting of EFW should be done on reference chart to determine centile.
-Universal growth harts should be adjusted according to local data.
-Amniotic fluid estimation either by, SDP (2 – 8cm), or AFI (5 – 25cm).

 

⇨Uterine Artery Doppler:
-Predictive value of abnormal uterine artery Doppler is limited.
-Can be used along mid trimester anomaly scan (18 – 24 + 6 weeks) to determine abnormal placentation & therefore risk of early onset FGR also & early onset pre – Eclampsia.

Also help in determining growth surveillance pathway.

-Assessment of uterine Artery Pulsatility index is recommended.
-Assessment of uterine notching is not recommended as it is a qualitative assessment and it is common to have notching in 1st 43% notching in 2nd has similar sensitivity to PI.
-Uterine artery Doppler in 3rd helps in determining whether FGR is due to abnormal placentation & it has moderate role in predicting adverse outcome for SGA.
⇨placental biomarkers.
-Improve diagnostic of USG for SGA & SB.
-placental growth factor PIGF. & soluble fms – like tyrosine kinase (s – flt) are recommended for diagnostic of pre – Eclampsia and placental dysfunction. But these are not recommended in non – hypertensive FGR diagnosis.
-More useful in 3rd placental .
⇨Placental morphology/ Biometry.

Under research.

⇨Doppler Studies.
1.Umbilical Artery Doppler:
-In all growth restricted pregnancies.
-Reduces hospital admissions, neonatal mortality and pre – Term birth.

Abnormal can be defined as PI above 95th centile, absent diabolic flow reverse flow.

2.Ductus venous Doppler:
-Done if absent/ Reverse umbilical artery Doppler.
-In pre – Term FGR.
-Can be defined as raised PIV above 95th centile (pre – critical) or reverse wave (critical).
3.Cerebral Doppler:

Abnormal MCA CPR/ UCR can inform monitoring strategies but don’t determine timing of birth before 37 weeks, but after 37 weeks it ca guide about timing of birth.

Management of FGR:

•AEDF on UAD in Early FGR:
-Try to prolong till 34 weeks.
-Deliver by 34 weeks.
-Consider delivery by 32 weeks.
•REDF on UAD in early FGR:
-Try to prolong till 32 weeks.
-Deliver by 32 weeks.
-Consider by 30 weeks.

Referral to FMU:

1.EFW < 3rd centile.
2.EFW < 10th centile + abnormal uterine artery Doppler.
⇨Invasive testing:
1.Severe SGA + structural anomalies (offered).
2.SGA + structurally normal features before 23 weeks + normal uterine artery Doppler (considered).

Analysis includes:

1.Micro array to detect micro insertions & micro deletions.
2.Pre – natal exome sequencing should only be considered in cases with multi system abnormalities or isolated short long bones.

 

⇨Serological Screening of Infections:
-Incidence of FGR due to infections is 5%.

Causative Agents:

-CMV, toxoplasmosis, malaria, syphilis
-Full TORCH screening is not recommended
-Testing should be based on presentation and history.
1.CMV: Testing should be offered in severe SGA.
2.Malaria: offered to those who have travelled in endemic areas. It is a significant cause of PTB and LBW.
3.Zika Virus: FGR is seen in 10% of infected women and is femur sparing pattern of FGR testing is offered to high-risk population.

Treatment or interventions for FGR:

•No proven intervention except birth of baby.
•LMWH no role.
•Phosphodiesterase 5 inhibitors – no proven role.

 

 

Birth of FGR/ SGA:

Pre – Term FGR:

•Involvement of MDT:
1.Obstetrician.
2.Neonatologist.
3.Fetal medicine if birth before 28 weeks.
•In – utero Transfer – if non availability of cot.
•Steroid cover – offer 24 – 34 + 6 weeks.

Reduces neonatal death, RDS and perinatal death.

•Effective between 48 hours to 7 days of administration.
•MgSO4 – offer @ 24 – 29 + 6 weeks, consider @ 30 – 33 + 6 weeks reduces neurological developmental abnormalities.

Mode of Birth:

C – section is recommended in:

1.Abnormal CCTG.
2.DV Doppler alteration.
3.Absent diastolic flow.
4.Reverse diabolic flow.

IOL is offered if:

1.SGA.
2.Late FGR with (N) umbilical artery Doppler.
3.Late FGR abnormal umbilical artery PI.
-There is risk of emergency C/section in IOL & need for continuous fetal monitoring.
-Consider mechanical methods of induction.

Spontaneous Labor:

-Early admission in labor.
-Continuous fetal heart rate monitoring.
-SGA/ FGR fetuses’ area @ ed risk of hypoxia suspected fetal compromise and late deceleration on CTG.

Postnatal investigations:

•Placental histopathology.
-Useful in FGR to plan future pregnancies.
•Postnatal Counselling.
-Proper appointment after birth.
-Aim of appointment is to discuss histopathology report and underlying causes as appropriate like APLS.
•Planning for future Pregnancy.
-Planning + preventive strategies like smoking cessation, Aspirin treatment, weight management (if needed).
